blocks.text: Dimensional method (tareeqa) yeh nahi bata sakta ke equation mein ghalti kahan hai. Agar equation dimensionally correct nikle, tab bhi hum sirf itna keh sakte hain ke equation sahi ho sakti hai, kyunke yeh method numerical factors ya constants (jaise ½ ya 2π) ko check nahi karta. Yeh sirf experiment se ya variables ka suitable (munasib) graph bana kar maloom hota hai.

blocks.prompt: Check karein ke v² = vᵢ² + 2aS dimensionally correct hai, aur dimensions se dikhayein ke simple pendulum ka time period T = constant × √(ℓ/g) hai.
blocks.explanation: [v²] = [LT⁻¹]² = [L²T⁻²]; [vᵢ²] bhi yahi; [aS] = [LT⁻²][L] = [L²T⁻²]. Har term ki dimension [L²T⁻²] hai, is liye equation homogeneous hai. Pendulum: T = (constant) ℓᵃgᵇ lein: [T] = [L]ᵃ[LT⁻²]ᵇ = [Lᵃ⁺ᵇ T⁻²ᵇ]. To a + b = 0 aur −2b = 1, yani b = −½, a = ½. Is liye T = constant × ℓ¹ᐟ² g⁻¹ᐟ² = constant × √(ℓ/g). Constant (2π) dimensions se nahi milta.

blocks.caption: Common (aam) quantities ki dimensions
rows: length, depth, height, diameter, light year

items: Homogeneity: sahi equation ke dono taraf dimensions ek jaisi (S = ½at² se [L] = [L]); numerical factors ki dimension nahi.
Derivation: F = (constant) mᵃvᵇrᶜ se a = 1, b = 2, c = −1, yani F = mv²/r. Limitation: constants aur ghalti ki jagah check nahi hoti.
